title: Basis.orthonormalized() may return axis of length 0.99999994039536 instead of 1.0
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: - 4.4.1.stable - master [99f5a3d] ### System information Godot v4.1.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop - Intel i7-12700H (20 threads) ### Issue description After Basis.rotated(), Basis.orthonormalized() may return a basis with at least one axis of length 0.99999994039536 instead of 1.0 ([as the Doc suggests](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_basis.html#class-basis-method-orthonormalized)). This is fixable by manually calling Vector3.normalized() on each axis afterwards. Notes: - Vector3.normalized() seems to return the same vector coordinates, but the vector length gets corrected to 1.0 - When discovering an axis with 0.99999994039536, rotating the camera once and then back (e.g. pitch up and then pitch down) will usually correct the length to 1.0 ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the attached project and run it in the editor 2. Use W S, A D, Q E to rotate the camera 3. After rotating in the same direction several times (e.g. pitch up), the Basis.orthonormalized() function may return a basis with at least one axis of length 0.99999994039536 instead of 1.0 ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp_orthonormalized.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20429632/mrp_orthonormalized.zip)
